name: Ansus
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.note: Yapen Austronesian (Indonesia); only classification/wordlist material (Anceaux 1961) located; no phonology or stress description found.

new_statements.quote: In addition to these segmental units, there is also contrastive stress in the language, which is not found in Ambai. The syllable structure is not complicated, and there is no evidence of suprasegmental systems operating other than contrastive stress. [...] One important phonological, but not orthographic, difference between Ansus and Ambai is that Ansus has phonologically contrasting stress.
new_statements.citation: Price, David S. & Mark Donohue. 2009. Report on the Ansus survey, West Yapen Island, Papua, Indonesia. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001. Dallas: SIL International.
new_statements.locator: Appendix IV: Phonological statement, p. 22 (PDF p. 22 of 25)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: ./pomm1237/ copy; pdfinfo: Price & Donohue, SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-001, 35 pages, not 25 as the citation/locator say -- the wordlist runs pp. 22-35). extracted text of printed p. 22 = PDF p. 22, 'Appendix IV: Phonological statement', contains verbatim: 'In addition to these segmental units, there is also contrastive stress in the language, which is not found in Ambai. The syllable structure is not complicated, and there is no evidence of suprasegmental systems operating other than contrastive stress.' and, after Tables 3-4 (12 consonants, 5 vowels) and the orthography remark, 'A more complete phonological statement is in preparation. One important phonological, but not orthograph…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is phonologically contrastive (lexically distinctive) in Ansus; the source gives no default position, no rule and no minimal pairs, only that stress contrasts exist, that there is no tone or other suprasegmental system, and that this distinguishes Ansus from Ambai. A fuller phonological statement was announced as 'in preparation' and has not been located.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated. Silzer 1983 (Ambai, Appendix A pp. 236-237) adds second-hand that Yapen languages including Ansus have two verb-stem classes, stem-initial syllable stressed vs unstressed, visible in infix morphophonemics.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level phonological statement based on wordlists elicited in Ansus and Warabori villages (March 2002) plus David Price's later contact with Ansus speakers; the Appendix V wordlist itself carries no stress marks.
new_statements.identity_note: Language-level ansu1237 / ISO and. Price & Donohue 2009 describe 'Ansus' from wordlists elicited in Ansus village (Kampung Ansus, West Yapen) and Warabori (March 2002) plus Price's later contact; Warabori is listed by Anceaux 1961 (p. 6) as a Marau-dialect village, but the phonological statement is presented as Ansus proper. Not to be confused with Anus [auq] (Sarmi coast).

sources.note: Appendix IV 'Phonological statement' (p. 22): 12 C + 5 V; 'there is also contrastive stress in the language, which is not found in Ambai'; 'no evidence of suprasegmental systems operating other than contrastive stress'; 'Ansus has phonologically contrasting stress'. No position rule, no minimal pairs; 'A more complete phonological statement is in preparation.' Appendix V wordlist (pp. 22-25) unmarked for stress.
